newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Germany's Leipziger buys 49 pct of Russian insurer.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Leipziger buys 49 pct of Russian insurer.

text.p: German insurer Alte Leipziger Versicherung AG said on Wednesday it had bought 49 percent of Russian property and casualty insurer RUSS of St Petersburg.
The company also announced that "not later than 1997" it will set up a life insurance company in Russia together with its Russian partners.

Hans-Dieter Knuettel, management board member of Alte Leipziger, Oberursel, told Reuters on Wednesday that a further western insurer -- "possibly from Scandinavia" -- might become a shareholder of the new life company.

Alte Leipziger, via its subsidiary Alte Leipziger Europa Beteiligungsgesellschaft mbH, acquired 49 percent of RUSS Insurance by picking up all shares issued in a capital increase, doubling RUSS' share capital from 1.5 billion roubles to 3 billion roubles (820,000 marks).
Majority owner of RUSS remains Vladislav Reznik, the company's founder, who is meanwhile also chairman of government-owned insurer Rosgostrakh, Moscow.
Knuettel declined to specify the exact sum his company had to pay. Alte Leipziger manager Roland Lenz has been appointed chief executive of RUSS.

The Russian insurer was set up in 1990, as one of the country's first privately-owned insurance companies. It had premium volume of sixmillion marks in 1995, both from industrial and commercial business as well as from motor (green card) and foreign travel health insurance. RUSS has some 100 staff and agents.

Alte Leipziger, a medium-sized German insurance group with 4.3 billion marks premium income and 3,900 staff, has been active in eastern Europe since 1991. It has joint ventures or subsidiaries in Lithuania, Estonia, Latvia, Belarus, Poland and the Russian enclave around Kaliningrad.

The company cooperates, among others, with German reinsurer Munich Re, which is a 15 percent shareholder in Estonian life insurer BICO Life (Balti Kindlustusselts Baltic Insurance Company). Alte Leipziger owns the majority of BICO Life.
The eastern European companies reached 80 million marks premium income in 1995 and are set to top 100 million marks this year.
